extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys, agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidelines for preparing Office actions, communicating with applicants, citing prior art, furnishing copies of cited references, and handling electronic retrieval/formatting of cited materials during patent examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include identifying numbers on replies to Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies to Office actions should include the application number as well as the 4-digit art unit number and the examiner’s name; applicants are encouraged to include the 4-digit confirmation number on every paper filed in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §503 for explanation of the confirmation number; including these identifiers expedites handling within the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reasons and references for rejections/objections (35 U.S.C. 132)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever any claim is rejected or any objection is made, notification of the reasons for rejection/objection together with such information and references as may be useful in judging the propriety of continuing the prosecution should be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When necessary, include particular figures, pages, or paragraphs of references and any brief relevant comments; be explicit in 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections how a reference is modified or how plural references are combined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary explanation may be required in exceptional or pro se cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In exceptional cases, and in pro se cases where the inventor is unfamiliar with patent law and practice, a more complete explanation may be needed to satisfy 37 CFR 1.104(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide more detailed explanation of rejections/objections and references for lay inventors so prosecution is understandable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Action Summary (PTOL‑326) as first page; attachments part of action
rubrics_metrics.description: Office Action Summary form PTOL-326 serves as the first page of the Office action (a Form PTOL-90 may be used as a coversheet) and will identify any allowed claims; attachments have the same paper number and are to be considered part of the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure PTO forms are included and properly numbered so the file wrapper records the Office action and attachments coherently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use form paragraphs 7.100, 7.101, or 7.102 to conclude actions
rubrics_metrics.description: One of form paragraphs 7.100, 7.101, or 7.102 should conclude all actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These form paragraphs supply standardized contact/closure language for Office actions and should be used to conclude communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.100 — Name And Number of Examiner To Be Contacted
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a sentence directing inquiries concerning the communication to a named examiner and telephone number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the paragraph, insert the name of the examiner designated to be contacted and the individual area code and phone number of that examiner (may be non-signatory or signatory examiner).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.101 — Telephone Inquiry Contacts (non 5/4/9 schedule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contact name, telephone number, days the examiner works, normal duty hours, and supervisor contact if examiner cannot be reached; include PAIR access info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert name, phone, workdays (e.g., 'Monday-Thursday'), duty hours (e.g., '6:30 AM - 5:00 PM'), SPE name and SPE phone. Include PAIR URL and EBC contact info as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.102 — Telephone Inquiry Contacts (5/4/9 schedule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contact name, telephone number, normal duty hours, alternate reachability, supervisor contact info, and PAIR access info tailored for 5/4/9 schedule examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert name, phone, work days, duty hours (e.g., '6:30 AM - 4:00 PM'), compressed day off, SPE name and SPE phone, and EBC contact info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required citation data for domestic and foreign patents and publications
rubrics_metrics.description: If domestic patents are cited, state their numbers and dates and names of patentees; if U.S. patent application publications are cited, state publication number, publication date, and names of applicants; if foreign published applications or patents are cited, give nationality/country, numbers, dates, and patentee names; for printed publications give author (if any), title, date, pages or plates, and place of publication or where a copy can be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where only part of a foreign document is involved identify particular pages and sheets; include other data necessary to enable identification by applicant or patent owner in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit support when rejection based on Office employee's personal knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: When a rejection is based on facts within the personal knowledge of an employee of the Office, the data shall be as specific as possible, and the reference must be supported, when called for by the applicant, by the affidavit of such employee, subject to contradiction or explanation by affidavits of the applicant and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure specifics are provided and be prepared to support factual assertions with affidavits when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite prior art nearest to claimed subject matter and explain pertinence
rubrics_metrics.description: During examination or reexamination the examiner should cite appropriate prior art which is nearest to the subject matter defined in the claims and, when such prior art is cited, its pertinence should be explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider all prior art references alone and in combination, including those cited by the applicant in a properly submitted IDS (MPEP §609). Form paragraph 7.96 may be used as an introductory sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.96 — Citation of Relevant Prior Art (introductory sentence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.96 states that prior art made of record and not relied upon is considered pertinent to applicant’s disclosure; when cited its relevance should be explained in bracketed text in accordance with MPEP §707.05.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bracketed explanation per MPEP §707.05 to set out relevance when including this paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisory oversight for third+ actions and long-pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisory patent examiners should ensure best references are found on the first search; they are expected to personally check pendency of every application up for the third or subsequent Office action and study applications pending five years to make every effort to terminate prosecution (consider such applications 'special').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impress assistants with shortest path to final disposition; apply focused review to applications with multiple actions or long pendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include citations for printing in allowed applications; record 'None' when no art found
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed applications should generally contain a citation of pertinent prior art for printing in the patent; only if a proper search has not revealed any prior art relevant to the claimed invention is it appropriate to send an application to issue with no art cited — in that case the examiner must write 'None' on form PTO-892 and insert it in the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When references have been cited during prosecution of parent and continuing applications, list the parent citations on form PTO-892 and place it in the file of the continuing application; in 37 CFR 1.53(d) continuation apps a new PTO-892 is not necessary if parent form is in same file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search based on actual U.S. filing date, not parent's filing date when benefit claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should search all applications based on the actual U.S. filing date of the application rather than on the filing date of any parent U.S. application for which benefit is claimed, due to 20-year patent term rules (Public Law 103-465).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware applicants may cancel benefit/priority claims by amending specification; ensure search uses correct effective filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite material prior art effective between parent filing and actual filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should cite as of interest all material prior art having an effective filing date after the filing date of the U.S. parent application but before the actual filing date of the application being examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include such references in the record where pertinent to patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing copies: foreign patent documents and NPL provided; U.S. patents and US app pubs not furnished in paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of cited foreign patent documents and non-patent literature are automatically furnished without charge to applicant together with the Office action; copies of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications are not provided in paper to applicants and are not placed in the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions exist (see points A–E) where copies are not furnished; examiner should check PTO-892 left-hand column to determine whether copy is to be furnished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions where copies of cited documents are not provided to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of documents cited by the examiner will be provided to applicant except where the documents: (A) are cited by applicant in accordance with MPEP §609/§707.05(b)/§708.02; (B) have been referred to in applicant’s disclosure statement; (C) are cited and provided in a parent application; (D) are cited by a third party in a 37 CFR 1.99 submission; or (E) are U.S. patents or U.S. application publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP §707.05(e) regarding data used in citing references to determine furnish/non-furnish status.

rubrics_metrics.name: At allowance furnish and retain copies of foreign patent docs and NPL cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of foreign patent documents and non-patent literature which are cited by the examiner at the time of allowance will be furnished to applicant with the Office action, and copies of the same will also be retained in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to all allowance actions, including first-action allowances and Ex Parte Quayle actions; for IFW processing see IFW Manual section 3.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for preparing/placing PTO‑892 and handling references
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist in providing copies or access to references the examiner should: (A) type the citation on form PTO-892 using OACS; (B) place PTO-892 in front of file wrapper; (C) include in the file wrapper all references to be furnished to the applicant; (D) turn the application in to technical support for counting (applications without required references will be returned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing references should be obtained and the file returned quickly; for IFW processing see IFW Manual section 3.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply same procedures to design applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of design applications, procedures are the same as set forth in MPEP §707.05 (a)-(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure citation/furnishing and PTO-892 handling are followed for design as well as utility/plant applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-Patent Reference access and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications are available free from the USPTO web site and via the E-Patent Reference feature on Private PAIR; access requires Private PAIR login which in turn requires a PKI digital certificate, a customer number associated with registration number, and installation of free software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: obtain a notarized PKI digital certificate, get a Customer Number (PTO-SB/125), associate registration number, install EFS/Private PAIR software, ensure Internet access (high-speed recommended); applicants/unrepresented practitioners are urged to follow these steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-submitted citations do not relieve examiners of independent search obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted citations by applicants will not in any way diminish the obligation of examiners to conduct independent prior art searches or relieve examiners of citing other pertinent prior art they may be aware of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant-submitted citations in accordance with MPEP §609 will not be supplied with an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for applicant-submitted information (37 CFR 1.105 / MPEP §704.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may require applicants to submit information reasonably necessary for the Office to examine an application or treat a matter being addressed; any such requirement and information submitted in reply will not diminish examiner obligations and will not be supplied with an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedures set forth in 37 CFR 1.105 and MPEP §704.10 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of listing references on PTO‑892
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing references for the first time, place identifying data on PTO-892 (a copy attached to the Office action); no distinction is to be made between references on which a claim is rejected and those formerly referred to as 'pertinent'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for applicant submitted citations, it is recommended that the pertinent features of references not used as a basis for rejection be briefly pointed out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite applicant-referred references on PTO‑892 when relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant in an amendatory paper refers to a reference that is subsequently relied upon by the examiner, such reference shall be cited by the examiner using form PTO-892 unless the applicant has listed the reference on form PTO/SB/08 initialed by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper citation procedure when converting applicant-cited references into examiner-cited references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data required when citing U.S. patent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If a U.S. patent application publication is cited, include publication number, publication date, name of the applicant, class, and subclass; for U.S. patents include patent number, patent date, name of the patentee, class and subclass; examiners are encouraged to cite kind codes printed on publications and patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §901.04 for explanation of kind codes and patent series; note special rules (e.g., X-Series patents not cited by number).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite Invention Defensive Publications Registrations (SIRs) under U.S. patent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention Defensive Publications Registrations (SIRs) should be cited under the 'U.S. Patent Documents' section on PTO-892 (see MPEP §711.06(a) and §901.06(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include SIRs in same section as U.S. patent documents when preparing PTO-892.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data required when citing foreign patents and published applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing foreign patents, include the patent number, kind code, citation date, country name, patentee name, and U.S. class/subclass if appropriate; if Technology Centers filing by IPC were used, cite the IPC subclass/group/subgroup on the file wrapper and PTO-892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow IFW processing conventions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing books: identify specific pages/sheets when only part relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: For books, where less than the entire disclosure is relied upon, the sheet and page numbers specifically relied upon and the total number of sheets/pages must be included (except applicant-submitted citations); if the entire disclosure is relied on, total number of sheets/pages are not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle similar foreign-language allowed applications and printed specifications accordingly; include sufficient page/sheet info to locate the relied portion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite non-patent publications with sufficient bibliographic information
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts, abbreviatures, Alien Property Custodian publications, withdrawn patents, and other non-patent documents should be cited under 'Non-Patent Documents' on PTO-892; provide sufficient information to determine identity and facilitate location (e.g., author, title, date, pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For books, author/title/date suffice when full details unavailable; STIC call numbers may be used for items owned by STIC but the call number itself SHOULD NOT be cited in the patent text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not abbreviate titles of books and periodicals
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles of books and periodicals SHOULD NOT be abbreviated because an abbreviation may be insufficient to identify the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full title, volume/issue/date/pages for periodicals; minimal citations allowed only if complete bibliographic details are unknown or unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include identification number and class/subclass when citing NPL with document ID
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a nonpatent literature reference with a document identification number is cited, the identification number and the class and subclass should be included on form PTO-892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format provided in MPEP: include ID and class/subclass entries to aid retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain photocopy of portions of outside publications relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original publication is located outside the Office, the examiner should immediately make or order a photocopy of at least the portion relied upon and indicate the class and subclass in which it will be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that the relied-upon material is preserved in the Office file for future reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and citation requirements for electronic documents (WIPO ST.14 alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow WIPO ST.14 recommended format for electronic documents: make format analogous to paper citation and add (A) type of electronic medium in square brackets (e.g., [online], [CD-ROM]); (B) date retrieved in square brackets (YYYY); (C) 'Retrieved from' and address; (D) DOI or other unique identifier if known; (E) standard identifier like ISBN/ISSN if known; (F) indicate format when multiple renderings exist (e.g., PDF, HTML); (G) use paragraph/sentence/line numbers to describe specific location; (H) include claim/figure/formula/sequence numbers where available; (I) indicate specific headings if pagination not available; (J) indicate specific passages when pagination or internal referencing exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples are provided (documents from online databases, Internet, electronic serials). Retain office copies where electronic sources may not be available later. If also available in paper form, it need not be identified as electronic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain Office copies for electronic documents that may not be retrievable later
rubrics_metrics.description: Office copies of an electronic document must be retained if the same document may not be available for retrieval in the future (important for Internet and online databases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve such copies in the file wrapper to ensure future access and reproducibility of the cited material.
